Analysis and Prevention of Biological Air Pollution in Sterile Biochemical Product Manufactures, Surgical Theaters and Sensitive Oncological Units

Results from the microbiological examination of air samples taken from air where sterile biochemical products are prepared were compared to the valid FDA standards. Methods of microbiological examinations of air, surface and material samples from sensitive surgery theaters are described and the results were evaluated. Preliminary guidelines for bacteriological standards for surgical theaters are proposed.
The methods for detection of molds, yeasts, mainly Aspergillus fumigatus, A. niger, A. flavus, and A. terreus causing invasive Aspergillosis-an airborne fatal infection in oncology and bone marrow transplant units are described and the results of the examinations are analyzed. Preliminary microbiological standards in the air of the described units are proposed.
The aim of the work was to achieve an environment where sterile biochemical products can be prepared and the occurrence of airborne secondary surgical infections and invasive Aspergillosis among patients are prevented.
